reason: The crank and ratchet wheel look like they belong on the winding drum before it is installed.
expectation: The crank and ratchet will attach to the drum to make a winding mechanism.

effect: The crank and drum form a hand winch, ready to be fitted to the crane.
reaction: The trade-off between turning effect and hand travel is interesting.
reason: The crane needs the winch to wind its lifting cord.
expectation: The hand winch will attach to the crane frame.

effect: The winch is installed, so the crane can now be rigged for lifting.
reason: The cord and hook should connect the winch to a load through the tip pulley.
expectation: The cord and hook will be fitted to the crane.

effect: The lifting line is fitted, leaving the crane to be made secure and tested.
reason: The pawl and release lever should let the ratchet hold a raised load and release it for lowering.
expectation: The holding and release mechanism will be fitted to the crane.

effect: The pawl can hold the line but does not prevent the crane tipping, so the crane needs stability before testing.
reaction: The distinction between holding the rope and preventing tipping is useful.
reason: The rear ballast should help counter the load at the boom before a lifting test.
expectation: The ballast will attach to the rear of the crane to improve its stability.

effect: The ballast and pawl are fitted, and the crane is ready for a low test of both.
reaction: Testing the two safety features together makes sense.
reason: The padded test weight is the appropriate load for the low test before lifting the basket.

choice.with: Ballasted holding crane ready for a test

expectation: The crane will lift and hold the test weight low down so its stability and pawl can be checked.

effect: The low test showed that the feet stay down and the pawl catches the drum; lowering requires holding the crank while easing the release.
reaction: The distinction between holding and controlled release is useful.
reason: The crane has passed its low test, so the cargo basket is the next load to try.
expectation: The crane will lift, hold and gently lower the basket.

effect: The basket test completed the goal and showed the pawl holding the load while the crank and release controlled its descent.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the separate holding and lowering mechanisms work together.

mostWorthwhile.text: The low test was most worthwhile: it showed both how the pawl catches the drum and why the crank must be held during release.

leastWorthwhile.text: Installing the winch and lifting line was straightforward but less informative than testing the finished mechanism.

surprise.text: The pawl can prevent the drum from unwinding but cannot prevent the crane itself from tipping; ballast addresses a different problem.

arbitrary.text: No action felt especially arbitrary; each part had a clear role in the lift or its test.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the low test and controlled basket lift made the construction feel purposeful while explaining useful mechanical distinctions.
